messages.content: What is a Wilson lower bound and why use it instead of a raw agreement rate for the router?

content.text: A Wilson lower bound is a confidence-interval estimate of a proportion that accounts for sample size: with few observations it sits well below the raw rate, and it converges to the raw rate as n grows. Using it instead of the raw agreement rate means a category with only a handful of agreeing replays cannot look routable just by chance.
